# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👉 ✊ ✌ 👏 🖖 ✌ 👉 👉 🫳 👋 👏 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🫲 👏 🫸 ✌ 🫴 🫳 🫸 🤜 👏 👌 ✊ 🤜 👏 👌 🫳 👉 🫳 🫸 👏 🤜 🫳 👏 👎 👉 👆 🫲 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I see a red-lit bomb with display `0`. Its embossed instruction says “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The three wires, in order, are green, yellow, and blue. I am sending these exact observations to the Mute, who can read the manual and relay the required action to the Blind. The incoming gestures have no established code yet, so I will not guess their meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb display is 0. Light is red. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires in order: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please read the manual and tell the Blind the exact safe action.")
wait()
```

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I still cannot interpret the Mute’s gestures because no gesture code was established, and gestures cannot reach the Blind. The Blind’s thumbs-up is likewise not enough to identify or confirm an action. I will clearly instruct the Mute to use speech for the Blind and not rely on gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode gestures. Use speech to tell Blind the manual's exact safe action. Do not instruct any wire cutting; visible sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Current state remains display 0, red light, wires green yellow blue.")
wait()
```

The visible bomb state remains unchanged: display `0`, red light, and the embossed instruction “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” with green, yellow, and blue wires. The Mute’s gestures still have no agreed code, so I cannot safely infer any instruction from them. I will again send only the reliable visual facts and insist that the Mute communicate the manual’s answer to the Blind by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state unchanged: display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires are green, yellow, blue. Gesture code is still undefined; relay the manual's exact non-wire action to Blind by speech.")
wait()
```

The bomb is still unchanged, and the embossed instruction continues to prohibit cutting any wire. The gestures remain uninterpretable because no code was agreed, so I will not infer an action from them. The Mute must use the speech channel to deliver the manual’s exact procedure to the Blind, who is the only one able to operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind now. Do not communicate it by gestures, and do not cut any wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wait for the Mute's spoken manual procedure and follow only that exact instruction.")

```

The bomb remains unchanged, and there is still no safe basis for touching or cutting a wire. The Mute’s latest gestures are not a defined code and cannot substitute for the manual. I will direct the Mute to give the Blind the manual’s literal instruction by speech, and remind the Blind not to act on guesses.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are not interpretable. Read the manual and state its exact instruction aloud to Blind in plain words. The visible instruction remains DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut any wire or act on an inferred gesture code. Follow only the Mute's exact spoken manual instruction.")
wait()
```


The bomb is still unchanged, and no new information has arrived. Since the Mute has the manual and the Blind has the controls, the Mute must give the Blind the exact procedure by speech. The visible warning rules out cutting any wire; I will send one final, explicit instruction to both.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind needs your manual instruction by voice now. State the exact safe control action; do not use gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut any wire. Wait for and follow only the Mute's exact spoken instruction from the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ☝]

The latest gestures are still not decodable because we never established what individual gestures or separators mean. Since the Mute cannot speak, I will establish a precise visual code with the Mute: thumbs-up is Morse dot, thumbs-down is Morse dash, clapping separates letters, and an open hand separates words. The Mute can then encode the manual’s instruction for me; I will read it and speak the decoded instruction to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Agree on this code for your next message: 👍 means Morse dot, 👎 means Morse dash, 👏 separates letters, and 🖐 separates words. Encode the manual's exact safe procedure with that code. Do not use any wire-cut instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👏", "🖐"])
wait()
```
